I purchased this laptop in April 2026, and it soon began restarting randomly. The official Lenovo Diagnostics tool confirmed critical physical RAM failures (hardware errors during MOVING_INVERSIONS_32BIT and QUICK_RANDOM_PATTERN_TEST), causing severe data corruption and system instability. The system runs on a soldered Micron module and a secondary KINGBOX expansion module in slot DIMM0. To make matters worse, Lenovo's website states the laptop is already out of factory warranty, and Amazon no longer accepts returns due to the elapsed time. Beware of this hardware batch and check your warranty

The Amazon page claims that this does not come with a camera, but I can assure you that it does. This is my second Asus G16 system, the first of which I gave to my wife since her original laptop died. Other than some really superficial details, it is hard tell them apart at first glance. All in all I am glad I found the ROG line from Asus!

Great laptop BUT ships with bad default settings that cause crashes. BEFORE you think your PC is broken: 1. Set TDR timeout to 60 seconds (Google how to change TdrDelay in registry) 2. Go to Nvidia Control Panel → Set default GPU to your dedicated, not auto-select Do this DAY ONE or every game will crash and you’ll think you need to RMA. Hardware is amazing once you fix ASUS’s lazy configuration. Do better ASUS.”

Avoid this product.  It's the most disappointing laptop I've ever had. Tl;dr: The laptop mostly functions as expected, but there is something seriously wrong with the networking that I believe is software related.  This was fixed for me by reinstalling Windows.  The installation it came with had some kind of networking issue that I couldn't resolve without wiping the pre-configured drive. The other major issue is the keyboard malfunctions by periodically cutting out for 30 seconds at a time every 30 minutes or so.  This is kind of weird because I didn't have this issue initially. If you don’t live with other people or otherwise do your gaming (and other fan-triggering computations) in isolation, then put on good noise-isolating headphones and don’t worry about it. I use this laptop exclusively for AI/ML work in a professional setting — no gaming. Performance is outstanding and a clear step up from my previous Dell XPS 16 (i7, 64GB RAM, Nvidia 4GB). Tasks that used to drag now run smoothly and quickly. The fan is louder than I’d like, but the productivity gains far outweigh this minor drawback. The camera is good, and the microphone with Nvidia Broadcast is excellent for calls and recordings. The screen quality is very good; coming from OLED, I was worried, but I’ve been pleasantly surprised. The keyboard feels great, and I really like the layout. The power supply is quite large — not an issue for me, but worth noting if you travel often. Overall, this is an exceptional machine for professional AI/ML workloads.

The laptop works, but I was disappointed with the physical condition upon arrival. The device had visible damage/cracking near the hinge area straight out of the box. Since this is a renewed/refurbished business laptop, I expected some cosmetic wear, but structural damage around the hinge was not expected. The listing did not clearly show this condition, and hinge cracks are concerning because they can worsen over time with normal use. Packaging could also have been better to protect the device during shipping. Performance-wise the laptop seems okay so far, but buyers should be aware that “renewed” may include noticeable chassis wear or previous stress damage. Overall: decent specs for the price, but quality control and cosmetic inspection should be improved.

review_excerpts: I came from the world of Thinkpads to fall for this Legion. I had (still have) a Lenovo Thinkpad X1 Extreme 2nd with i7-9750H, 64GB of RAM, 3TB of storage, 4K OLED touch panel and the GTX 1650 max-Q. I purchased this laptop in 2019 when it was announced (very pricey, but it was one of the best). It was very good at the beginning, but his thinness was a major flaw because it was overheating like hell with time passing. Since my work requires a powerhouse laptop with both the CPU and GPU, my laptops couldn't handle the workload anymore. I use a lot of virtualization labs and video rendering and it takes too much time to render one video session. So I looked for a replacement and found this Legion and I was quite impressed but a bit disappointed. Here are the pros and cons: Pros: - Very light

Beautiful screen, very fast/responsive, and handles high-end settings on most games. Battery life is great when just using it for business/work aspects off the charger, but it’s a gaming laptop at the end of the day. All pros from me with one con, the cooling fan is loud and kicks on with even routine use. If it keeps it cool, then I couldn’t care less.

I paid about $1,700 after tax for this Lenovo Legion 5i, and honestly, it’s beyond my expectations. The performance is smooth across everything I’ve tried — from everyday tasks to heavy gaming. The build feels solid, the cooling does a great job while keeping the fan noise really low  and the display is sharp and immersive. At this price point, I feel like it’s absolutely worth it. I ordered this touch screen, however, there's really nothing I need to touch as the mouse continues to be my choice.  It's got enough horsepower to do everything I do; email, finances, file storage, pic & video storage.  I bought this because my old Dell wouldn't upgrade to Win 11.  I was floating by on Microsoft's upgrade extension from last year and then here comes tax season and TurboTax required Win 11.  Oh well, I needed to upgrade at some point.  But, very happy with my new Dell!

The performance and available storage are good, however next time I would buy a different configuration. The configuration of the keyboard is odd. review_excerpts: This is a very fast and powerful computer.  I don’t game so I don’t speak to that aspect but it loads quickly and the apps run efficiently.  The graphics are clear and bright, the touch screen is responsive. You can spend a lot more for a computer that does not serve as well as this one.  I love that it has a restore usb, yes you have to be careful not to accidentally wipe your computer but you should never have the usb stick plugged in unless that is your intention.  I am totally pleased with this computer in every way.  I’ve never been disappointed with the Lenovo brand

Was super easy to set up and is fast I’ve been able to do light gaming the battery life is not very good I have to charge it like once a day but I also hardly turn it off it does charge in less than 30 mins so it’s not bad
love it..super slim, fast, and can handle all my task
Excelente muy buen equipo
The battery isn't that long. It said 6 to 7 hours, but I had to charge it twice one day. it lasts like for 3 hours and THAT'S IT.
I have owned only Lenovos for more than 15 years.  I have never had an issue with them, ever!

WHAT 4 stars for a great deal? The computer is a true bargain and quite impressive in every aspect. The only negative isn’t the computer it’s the 24H2 windows OS which purposely makes home networking close to impossible (it could be easy with a few simple coding changes) BUT I found a way to “back door” and get it working. Again great computer and if you aren’t home networking I see no issues for you. And the pricing for the product with the AMD chip is great. I’d do it again without question.
20gb of RAM is heaven. This machine boots up super fast, is lightweight, has a crazy-long charge, and was the best buy I found after several months of research. I'm very pleased.

review_excerpts: Came I recently got the Apple 2026 MacBook Air 15-inch with the M5 chip, and honestly it exceeded my expectations. I don't usually write reviews, but I recently bought this computer and I'm loving it. I previously had an M2 2023 Macbook Air that I got water in and fried. This essentially does all the same things, but cooler. It also has a bigger screen, which is perfect for me since I do a lot of work on my computer and constantly have a million tabs open. I'm also a student, so there's that. No complaints! The battery life is great and much better than my old computer. The color is a beautiful blue, which I've never seen before and I think is quite unique. I've gotten compliments on it. It also runs much faster and for some reason connects better to my crappy printer! Win all around!

Ordered via Prime and the Mac arrived the next day.  Setup was easy.  The M5 chip flies but my usage is basically routine functions no heavy usage.  Everything is speedy.  This computer is an upgrade from my 2017 MacBook Pro and a 2020 iMac.  Both of those old Macs are still functional.  I've been using Macs since the Apple IIC and II GS.  Over 35 years ago.  The keyboard is one of the best I've used.  I loved the 2017 MBP keyboard because if had a great feel.  Others since then were not comfortable until this keyboard on the MB Air.  Booting up is fast.  For me the battery will last for four days before recharging.  I really like the Mag Safe charger.  Easy on and easy off especially if you happen to forget you're charging and pull the computer away from the connection.  Connection just d

This is my first Mac. I was apprehensive to go from the PC world to the Mac world, but now I know I won't go back. The display is very bright and life-like. It almost makes me feel like I'm at the beach. Having never owned a Mac before, it has been a learning curve. The performance is fast. The weight was a little more than I wanted; however, I went with the 15-inch, so I knew it would be a little heavier. I love the 15-inch size as I can see everything better. The trackpad is a nice size, and the keys are light on the fingers.

I love my new laptop!  I replaced an older MacBook Pro with the Air. The MB Air is lightweight and runs so much cooler than my Pro did. I ordered it in the starlight color. Had second thoughts about not ordering the silver, but the color of the starlight is so close to the silver that it didn’t matter. The speed of the new machine is awesome. The purchase was worth every penny.

No more MS! Thats worth five stars there. Have had a little experience with early Apple systems and converted old laptops to Linux. I like all the features with the possible exception of the AI. Right now I am having a few minor issues with the scroll bars and split screen stuff but somewhere on this Mac is a menu to take care of it. I like the aluminum case and have had other plastic laptops that have had issues with broken plastic hinges that bind etc. I also like the lighted keyboard and am getting familiar with the rest of the system. Very quick with a bluetooth mouse. Much safer to shop with and surf the net,
This MacBook is quick and light weight. I love the bigger screen. I would highly recommend it for a college student or for home computer use.

review_excerpts: Apple never disappoints. They again made a most quality product. I had a Macbook pro from 2014 that became sluggish from a coffee spill. I can't easily transfer my data over to the new Macbook Air but I am still figuring that out and am not too worried about it. The Macbook Air is incredibly sleek and fast. I love typing on it, the fingerprint lock, 13 inch is the perfect screen size. I really love this computer and it has already brought me so much joy.

The Mac Book Air is what you expect from Apple:  excellent design and top notch technical specs. for it's price point. It's perfect for my use case (moderate photo and video editing).  It delivers on being a small form factor and light weight. Delivery was fast and efficient.

Absolutely perfect. Great battery life, great performance. I've got 1TB Storage capacity and it's perfect as well. I had M1 8/256 and this is perfect successor, but I can't say this has better design or speakers. Designewise M1 is flawless and better, but speakers . . . Speakers are tough. I think M1 has bit better speakers. In this case sound comes from front and it's much quieter, M1 is louder and sound comes from edges and it's perfect. In terms of sound quality, it's hard to tell, which sounds better. Screen is much better, keyboard is better, touchpad is better, fingerprint sensor is better. It's better every single way. Perfect product, absolutely love it
Awesome performance.  So much lighter than I expected.
So thin. So light. So powerful. Great look and feel. Best computer of its size in my opinion.
Nice Mac and price. Nice and light.
Beautiful and easy to setup
Upgrade from a MacBook Air M1 base model and the performance is great, WiFi speeds are also improved, also the 10GPU bump when you get 1tb is absolutely welcome. Midnight color is beautiful!!!

review_excerpts: I replaced my 6-year old HP Envy with this newer version and love it.  I've had is a few days and am learning about its newer features.  The fingerprint reader is great and makes it simpler to log in yet it is more secure in my opinion.  My old Envy was also a 17 inch screen version.  This laptop is slightly smaller overall but still has the same size screen.  It is also lighter that my old one.  The "M.2" solid state disk is fast and boot time is very quick.  I have configured most of the default storage locations to be on the second drive (a regular hard disk).  This machine is a great value for the money.

Very impressed with this laptop.  I almost didn't purchase another HP since the last laptop I had from them was a bit of a dog.  Fortunately I went ahead and got the Envy because of the features and good reviews.  I've had it now for 2 months and am very impressed. review_excerpts: Amazing laptop. The color I got didn't match the pics but I like what I received way better than the silver as advertised. Mine is like between a Navy Blue and a Black. The ASUS computers have been solid computers for mid tier gaming and designs. We have got several over the past few years. When choosing which one Get the CPU/GPU, graft a card, and screen size you want. You can upgrade memory and SSD to fit your goals. Based on others reviews I had seen some of the models sold by 3rd parties can potentially have some defects. But those seem hit or miss as any mass production item can have some faulty hardware. review_excerpts: I came from the world of Thinkpads to fall for this Legion. I had (still have) a Lenovo Thinkpad X1 Extreme 2nd with i7-9750H, 64GB of RAM, 3TB of storage, 4K OLED touch panel and the GTX 1650 max-Q. I purchased this laptop in 2019 when it was announced (very pricey, but it was one of the best). It was very good at the beginning, but his thinness was a major flaw because it was overheating like hell with time passing. Since my work requires a powerhouse laptop with both the CPU and GPU, my laptops couldn't handle the workload anymore. I use a lot of virtualization labs and video rendering and it takes too much time to render one video session. So I looked for a replacement and found this Legion and I was quite impressed but a bit disappointed. Here are the pros and cons: Pros: - Very light

Beautiful screen, very fast/responsive, and handles high-end settings on most games. Battery life is great when just using it for business/work aspects off the charger, but it’s a gaming laptop at the end of the day. All pros from me with one con, the cooling fan is loud and kicks on with even routine use. If it keeps it cool, then I couldn’t care less.

I paid about $1,700 after tax for this Lenovo Legion 5i, and honestly, it’s beyond my expectations. The performance is smooth across everything I’ve tried — from everyday tasks to heavy gaming. The build feels solid, the cooling does a great job while keeping the fan noise really low  and the display is sharp and immersive. At this price point, I feel like it’s absolutely worth it. The only area I’d suggest for improvement is RAM — the system is strong out of the box, but with more RAM it could unlock even more potential, especially for multitasking and future-proofing. Overall, I’m very satisfied and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, high-performance gaming laptop.

However, I was able to track down the poor performance to several Microsoft applications that start up automatically. The worst culprit was One-Drive which was continuously using about 60% of the CPU even when I was doing nothing on the computer. I used Task Manager - Startup to disable One Drive, Microsoft To Do, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Teams Personal, and Microsoft Power Automate Desktop, none of which are useful to me.
